items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: when we played in the trio, we played -- we did a duet date since we were recording a duet, we had Cliff Leeman on drums

ctx.x: But I am sure that he would be very tempted if he actually realized and knew that the things were at the stage that they are, I think he would be tempted.

Yes, just on the publicity he's gotten, you know, making a comeback and of course, the New Yorker article, which is a tremendous piece. That is big international stuff, I think he would get the greatest surprise of his life, because when we played in the trio, we played -- we did a duet date since we were recording a duet, we had Cliff Leeman on drums and Jess and Cliff didn't hit -- they didn't get on too well together, so we decided without offending Cliff, who is a super drummer, that we would do a session…

bers, we played Don't Blame Me as a ballad and some blues in F in a fast tempo, and I couldn't -- Jess got a standing ovation and I couldn't get him to stand up, he was so scared, but he played beautifully.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: he used Bud Freeman on tenor... we had the original which I mentioned, and then some dates he would add Billy Butterfield on trumpet and Peanut Hucko on clarinet or tenor, and he used Bud Freeman on tenor

ctx.x: But that band never had a bad moment in two or three years that I was playing down there off and on. This was downtown -- because I worked for 22 years off and on with Eddie Garner, which we'll get into later. But that band -- Bill and I are the only two people alive out of that one. For people who went there and felt and heard it -- and it was well known at the time -- we made a beautiful thing together. We made two albums for Columbia, I think you know -- they were picked two of the greatest all time jazz…

And we had two bands then, Eddie Condon -- used the house band for one set of a half hour for awhile, and then he'd switch over, and the guests would play, like Bill Butterfield, Bud Freeman -- do you understand what I'm getting at?
Of course, Cliff, I was there, too.
